 1          Pursuant to Local Rule 7-12, Plaintiffs Laura Perjanik, Samuel McClain, Victoria Tulsidas,

 2   Katrina McDowell, Jenny Ayoub, Tamir Sukkary, and Edina Cole and Defendant ProctorU, Inc.

 3   d/b/a Meazure Learning (collectively the “Parties”), through their respective attorneys, hereby

 4   stipulate and declare as follows:

 5          WHEREAS, the Parties have reached a class action settlement in principle and are

 6   executing a Term Sheet.

 7          WHEREAS, the Parties are currently memorializing their agreement via a Class Action

 8   Settlement Agreement and exhibits.

 9          WHEREAS, after the Parties finalize the Class Action Settlement Agreement and exhibits,

10   Plaintiffs intend to move for preliminary approval of the Class Action Settlement Agreement.

11          WHEREAS, to conserve the resources of the Parties who have resolved this action in

12   principle, the Parties agree that good cause exists to stay all scheduled deadlines, and to proceed

13   with deadlines related to approval of the forthcoming Class Action Settlement Agreement instead.

14          WHEREAS, the Parties further agree that the deadline for Plaintiff to file a motion for

15   preliminary approval should be September 11, 2026 to allow time to draft and execute the

16   agreement reached in principle and to prepare preliminary approval papers.

17          NOW THEREFORE, Plaintiffs and Defendant hereby agree and stipulate as follows:

18          1. All deadlines unrelated to approval of a class action settlement shall be stayed pending

19              approval of a class action settlement.

20          2. The deadline for Plaintiffs to file a motion for preliminary approval shall be September

21              11, 2026. The filing shall include further deadlines for the remainder of the action.

22

19           This is a class action lawsuit in which the plaintiffs allege that the defendant violated
20   California law in its administration of the February 2025 California Bar Examination. The parties
21   now enter the following Stipulation, subject to Court approval, to stay all proceedings so that they
22   may have a meaningful opportunity to attempt resolution of this matter through private mediation.
23   This is the first request for a stay of all proceedings.
24                                        Statement of Good Cause
25           The parties have agreed to mediate on July 14, 2026 before Hon. Andrew Guilford (Ret.).
26   To avoid incurring potentially unnecessary fees and costs relating to continued litigation and to
27   advance judicial economy so that the parties can focus on mediation and potential settlement of
28

 3          Defendant’s motion to dismiss is fully briefed and pending. The parties are also actively

 4   engaged in discovery. However, the parties agree it would be in their mutual interest to stay the

 5   case and engage in meaningful settlement discussions before the pending motion is decided. If the

 6   parties can resolve the case at this early juncture, they will preserve their own resources and

 7   promote judicial economy.

 8                                              Stipulation

 9          Accordingly, the parties HEREBY STIPULATE and request that the Court order as

10   follows:

11          1. The case, including all deadlines, is stayed pending the July 14, 2026 mediation

12              before Judge Guilford.

13          2. The parties shall file a joint status report on or before July 20, 2026 advising the

14              Court as to whether a settlement was reached.

                            UPDATED JOINT CASE MANAGEMENT STATEMENT
                                       Case No. 4:25-CV-2095
             Case 4:25-cv-02095-JST            Document 66         Filed 03/10/26      Page 2 of 12




 1   1.      Jurisdiction & Service

 2           This Court has subject matter jurisdiction over this action under the Class Action Fairness

 3   Act, 28 U.S.C. § 1332(d), as this is a class action in which at least some members of the proposed

 4   Class are citizens of a different State than Defendant and the claims of the proposed Class Members

 5   exceed $5,000,000 in the aggregate.

 6           Meazure was initially served with the complaint in the Perjanik and McDowell actions,

 7   and was served with the consolidated amended complaint via ECF on June 23, 2025.

 8   2.      Facts
 9           Plaintiffs’ Statement: Plaintiffs brought this action against ProctorU, Inc. d/b/a Meazure
10   Learning (“Meazure”), seeking relief individually and behalf of all those whose Bar Examinations
11   were disrupted because of Meazure’s software malfunction.
12           For the February 2025 Exam, the State Bar contracted with Meazure for the remote
13   proctoring software that test-takers were required to use to complete the exam on a computer.
14   Applicants who do not wish to handwrite the exam are required to use Meazure’s Platform and to
15   pay a fee to Meazure to take the test. Meazure knew well in advance how many thousands of
16   applicants would be taking the Exam, as thousands sign up for the CA Bar Exam each February
17   and each July. Meazure also knew how important the CA Bar Exam is for test takers. It understands
18   that the expenses associated with the test are significant, and that failure to pass the bar will prevent

19   law graduates from working as attorneys within the state of California.

20           Plaintiffs and Class Members invested significant time and money to prepare for the Exam.

21   They spent hundreds of hours studying, they invested in expensive test-preparation classes, and

22   they paid hefty fees to both the State Bar and to Meazure to take the Exam using its Platform. They

23   also spent time and money traveling to testing locations and taking practice tests to familiarize

24   themselves with the Platform. Despite the tremendous stakes associated with the CA Bar Exam,

25   on February 25 and 26, 2025, Meazure’s testing software crashed repeatedly during the Exam.

26   Meazure’s testing software crashed because it had insufficient infrastructure and/or lack of servers

27
                                                        2
                              UPDATED JOINT CASE MANAGEMENT STATEMENT
                                         Case No. 4:25-CV-2095
              Case 4:25-cv-02095-JST            Document 66      Filed 03/10/26      Page 3 of 12




 1   and server space to process the foreseeable number of exam takers. Meazure failed to design,

 2   maintain, and/or improve the infrastructure of the exam software to sufficiently and adequately

 3   service Plaintiffs and Class Members who had no choice but to pay Meazure’s fee to take the Exam

 4   on a computer.

 5           As a result of Meazure’s failure to have a properly functioning software available for

 6   applicants, Plaintiffs and the Class did not receive what they paid for – working test software that

 7   would let them complete one of the most important tests of their careers. Plaintiffs sat for the CA

 8   Bar Exam and suffered injury from these technical failures. Plaintiffs seek monetary redress and
 9   injunctive relief for themselves and the proposed Class who were injured when the February 2025
10   CA Bar Exam fell apart due to Meazure’s failures.
11           Defendant’s Statement: Meazure Learning contracted with the State Bar to administer
12   the February 2025 California bar exam. Meazure Learning did not contract with any of the
13   Plaintiffs, and none of the Plaintiffs paid any money to Meazure Learning. Further, Meazure
14   Learning denies that it made any actionable misrepresentation to any Plaintiff, and Meazure
15   Learning denies that it caused any Plaintiff any injury. Meazure Learning does not adopt or agree
16   to Plaintiffs’ recitation of the facts.
17   3.      Legal Issues

18           The legal issues include (1) whether Plaintiffs have adequately pled each of their claims;

19   (2) whether the proposed action can be maintained as a class action; (3) whether Defendant

20   Meazure is liable under any of the claims alleged in Plaintiffs’ complaint; and (4) whether

21   Plaintiffs are entitled to any damages, restitution, equitable, and/or injunctive relief as alleged in

22   Plaintiffs’ complaint.

23   4.      Motions

24           On October 6, 2025, Defendant filed its Motion to Dismiss Plaintiffs’ Consolidated

25   Amended Class Action Complaint [ECF No. 56]. The motion is fully briefed as of December 8,

26   2025.

27

                               UPDATED JOINT CASE MANAGEMENT STATEMENT
                                          Case No. 4:25-CV-2095
              Case 4:25-cv-02095-JST         Document 66        Filed 03/10/26      Page 4 of 12




 1           Plaintiffs’ Statement: Plaintiffs’ Motion to Consolidate Cases and Appoint Interim Lead

 2   Counsel was granted by the Court. Plaintiffs anticipate filing a motion for class certification, and

 3   possibly, a motion for summary judgment. It may also be necessary to file discovery motions and

 4   other pre-trial motions.

 5           Defendant’s Statement: Defendant anticipates filing a motion for summary judgment.

 6   Defendant will file discovery motions and other pre-trial motions as necessary.

 7   5.      Amendment of Pleadings

 8           Plaintiffs’ Statement: Plaintiffs filed their consolidated amended complaint on June 23,
 9   2025.
10           Defendant’s Statement: On October 6, 2025, Defendant filed its Motion to Dismiss
11   Plaintiffs’ Consolidated Amended Class Action Complaint [ECF No. 56].
12   6.      Evidence Preservation

13           The parties have reviewed the Guidelines Relating to the Discovery of Electronically

14   Stored Information (“ESI Guidelines”), and have confirmed they have met and conferred pursuant

15   to Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(f) regarding reasonable and proportionate steps taken to preserve evidence

16   relevant to the issues reasonably evidenced in this action.

17   7.      Disclosures

18           The parties served initial disclosures on June 10, 2025.

19   8.      Discovery

20           On September 3, 2025, Plaintiffs served their First Set of Requests for Production and First

21   Set of Interrogatories on Defendant. On September 19, 2025, Defendant served its First Discovery

22   Requests to Plaintiffs. The parties have responded to the discovery requests, and Plaintiffs have

23   produced documents. The parties are meeting and conferring regarding discovery.

24           On September 23, 2025, the Court entered the parties’ Stipulated Protective Order (ECF

25   53).

26

27

                                UPDATED JOINT CASE MANAGEMENT STATEMENT
                                           Case No. 4:25-CV-2095
             Case 4:25-cv-02095-JST           Document 66        Filed 03/10/26      Page 5 of 12




 1           Plaintiffs seek discovery including the following subjects: (i) Meazure’s exam testing

 2           This Court has subject matter jurisdiction over this action under the Class Action Fairness

 7   and was served with the consolidated amended complaint via ECF on June 23, 2025.

 8   2.      Facts
 9   Plaintiffs’ Statement: Plaintiffs brought this action against ProctorU, Inc. d/b/a Meazure Learning
10   (“Meazure”), seeking relief individually and behalf of all those whose Bar Examinations were
11   disrupted because of Meazure’s software malfunction.
12           For the February 2025 Exam, the State Bar contracted with Meazure for the remote
13   proctoring software that test-takers were required to use to complete the exam on a computer.
14   Applicants who do not wish to handwrite the exam are required to use Meazure’s Platform and to
15   pay a fee to Meazure to take the test. Meazure knew well in advance how many thousands of
16   applicants would be taking the Exam, as thousands sign up for the CA Bar Exam each February
17   and each July. Meazure also knew how important the CA Bar Exam is for test takers. It understands
18   that the expenses associated with the test are significant, and that failure to pass the bar will prevent

19   law graduates from working as attorneys within the state of California.

20           Plaintiffs and Class Members invested significant time and money to prepare for the Exam.

21   They spent hundreds of hours studying, they invested in expensive test-preparation classes, and

22   they paid hefty fees to both the State Bar and to Meazure to take the Exam using its Platform. They

23   also spent time and money traveling to testing locations and taking practice tests to familiarize

24   themselves with the Platform. Despite the tremendous stakes associated with the CA Bar Exam,

25   on February 25 and 26, 2025, Meazure’s testing software crashed repeatedly during the Exam.

26   Meazure’s testing software crashed because it had insufficient infrastructure and/or lack of servers

27

 1   and server space to process the foreseeable number of exam takers. Meazure failed to design,

 2   maintain, and/or improve the infrastructure of the exam software to sufficiently and adequately

 3   service Plaintiffs and Class Members who had no choice but to pay Meazure’s fee to take the Exam

 4   on a computer.

 5           As a result of Meazure’s failure to have a properly functioning software available for

 6   applicants, Plaintiffs and the Class did not receive what they paid for – working test software that

 7   would let them complete one of the most important tests of their careers. Plaintiffs sat for the CA

 8   Bar Exam and suffered injury from these technical failures. Plaintiffs seek monetary redress and
 9   injunctive relief for themselves and the proposed Class who were injured when the February 2025
10   CA Bar Exam fell apart due to Meazure’s failures.
11           Defendant’s Statement: Meazure Learning contracted with the State Bar to administer
12   the February 2025 California bar exam. Meazure Learning did not contract with any of the
13   Plaintiffs, and none of the Plaintiffs paid any money to Meazure Learning. Further, Meazure
14   Learning denies that it made any actionable misrepresentation to any Plaintiff, and Meazure
15   Learning denies that it caused any Plaintiff any injury. Meazure Learning does not adopt or agree
16   to Plaintiffs’ recitation of the facts.
